title: Try another rung only when nothing was sent; after a send, an absent effect is unknown
problem: A fallback that fires when the first route shows no effect cannot tell a silent no-op from an effect that lands late, so it can act twice.
mechanism: Each action returns a delivery outcome (not sent, sent, unknown) and an effect outcome (confirmed, absent at a declared bound, unreadable). Another rung may be tried automatically only when nothing was sent. After a send, an effect absent at the bound is an unknown outcome: no second dispatch, the typed outcome and escalation advice go to the caller. Sent with an unreadable effect blocks further mutation of that target until it is re-observed or acknowledged. Unknown delivery blocks all mutation in the domain and survives a crash.
when_to_use: Any surface where a route can report success without acting or can act late.
when_not_to_use: As a way to make progress unattended on surfaces whose first route often no-ops: this rule hands those cases to the caller. A later extension for absolute setters, whose mechanism yields the same state whether or not an earlier application lands, needs its own test.
tradeoffs: Stops more often than any reference chain. Wording a goal as a target state does not make its mechanism repeat-safe: a second click on a toggle flips it.
counterexample: The reference's right-click chain continues after unverified delivery, safe only because each step re-checks for an open menu. Its no-effect reading for selection sits inside a short settle window.

transfer.application: Write the nine-cell delivery-by-effect table before widening the browser lane, and carry the pinned driver's Confirmed and Unverifiable effect through browser_driver._effect. A driver Confirmed is a target-state reading and does not settle the business effect. Not implemented.
transfer.compatibility_checks: The CDP lane already blocks mutation after an acknowledged delivery with unverified effect; start --browser records delivery as unknown for every driver reply and has no crash-durable barrier.
transfer.next_test: A click-toggle whose effect lands after the bound, a lost acknowledgement, an acknowledged action with unreadable effect, and a restart mid-action: exactly one dispatch in each, and a block on further mutation in the last three.
